_note: Reviewed merges (from gemma's proposals in merge_proposals.json, with Claude's changes). 'groups' lists card ids to join, in order; text is joined by apply_merges.py with fixed rules, never taken from gemma. 'edits' are hand rewrites applied first, for cuts that cross a chapter or need a sentence boundary moved. 'exchanges' marks groups where joined quotes are different speakers (or a book being read aloud) and must stay separate quotes; elsewhere consecutive quotes are one speaker and become one quote. Per the user (2026-10-10), merges that put two different characters' lines on one card were dropped ('dropped_speaker_change').

ch_01/P0007.15.en: Look at Master Yi! He has a face like jade and looks like an immortal.
ch_01/P0007.15.ko: 도련님 모습을 보아라. 옥 같은 얼굴에 신선 같은 풍채로다.
ch_01/P0007.15.why: cut mid-sentence into the editorial bridge; split at a sentence boundary instead of merging into the bridge

ch_01/P0008.1.en: His long hair is neatly combed and braided. He wears fine silk clothes and a gat hat, and he looks like a proud young nobleman from the capital.
ch_01/P0008.1.ko: 긴 머리를 곱게 빗어 땋아 내리고, 고운 비단 옷에 갓을 받쳐 쓰니 한양 귀공자의 풍채가 늠름하다.
ch_01/P0008.1.why: second half of the split above

ch_13/P0006.13.en: "You say gisaeng can't be loyal or faithful, so I'll tell you about them one by one. Nongseon, a gisaeng from Hwanghae, died for her honor at Dongseon Pass.
ch_13/P0006.13.ko: "기생에게는 충효도 열녀도 없다 하시니, 하나하나 아뢰겠습니다. 황해도 기생 농선이는 동선령에서 죽어 이름을 남겼습니다.
ch_13/P0006.13.why: joining both halves goes over 300 characters; end the first half as a full sentence

ch_13/P0007.1.en: A little gisaeng in Seoncheon studied hard and became a scholar, and Nongae, the gisaeng of Jinju, gave her life for our country and is honored at a shrine to this day."
ch_13/P0007.1.ko: 선천 기생은 어린아이였지만 학문을 닦았고, 진주 기생 논개는 우리나라의 충렬로 충렬문에 모셔져 천년 제사를 받고 있습니다."
ch_13/P0007.1.why: second half, now a full sentence

ch_14/P0018.11.en: "Don't say such things. Let's just go to the prison." The guard carries Chunhyang on his back.
ch_14/P0018.11.ko: "그런 말씀 마시고 옥으로 가십시다." 사령이 춘향을 등에 업는다.
ch_14/P0018.11.why: chapter ended mid-sentence; ch_15 opens with the walk to the prison

ch_15/P0007.8.en: "Ghosts, if you want to take me, at least don't nag me about it." She chants a charm against ghosts and sits there.
ch_15/P0007.8.ko: "이 몸을 귀신들이 잡아가려거든 조르지나 말려무나." 하고 귀신 쫓는 주문을 외며 앉아 있다.
ch_15/P0007.8.why: chapter ended mid-sentence ('Outside the prison,'); the phrase moves to ch_16's first line

ch_16/P0002.1.en: A blind fortune-teller walks by outside the prison. A city fortune-teller would call out politely, but this is a country one, so he shouts, "Fortunes! Get your fortunes told!"
ch_16/P0002.1.ko: 옥 밖으로 점쟁이 봉사 하나가 지나간다. 서울 봉사 같으면 "문수(問數) 하오." 하련만, 시골 봉사라 "점 보시오!" 하고 외치며 간다.
ch_16/P0002.1.why: receives 'outside the prison' from the end of ch_15

ch_19/P0007.10.en: "and one day she'll fall asleep by the road and die, and the crows of Jirisan will come down and peck out her eyes, and she won't have a child to shoo them away."
ch_19/P0007.10.ko: "언덕 밑에서 쪼그리고 졸다가 지쳐 죽으면, 지리산 갈까마귀가 두 날개를 떨치고 내려와 두 눈을 다 파먹어도, 훠이 하고 쫓아 줄 자식 하나 없겠구나."
ch_19/P0007.10.why: move the end of her speech up so the next card starts with the inspector

ch_19/P0007.11.en: As she weeps, the inspector says, "Don't cry. Even if the sky falls, there's always a way out."
ch_19/P0007.11.ko: 아이고, 아이고, 서럽게 우니 어사또가 말한다. "울지 마라. 하늘이 무너져도 솟아날 구멍이 있느니라."
ch_19/P0007.11.why: now starts at a sentence boundary
